chapter: Postwar career: studio work, Kansas City, Europe
title: Studio session work behind other singers on the West Coast
summary: After the band folded he mostly recorded behind other artists for labels like Down Beat and Modern, at double pay, often uncredited.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Session players on the hits: "I played on that record"

blocks.x: Well, how long did you stay out on the coast that time?

Well, I stayed out -- I was out on the coast, I guess, about maybe a year and a half, and then the band went off. Then when the recording ban went off, well, then, most of the time that's what I was doing, recording behind other people, out there.
Oh, let's see, I think I -- who all did
I record behind? I think I did another session behind Spoon. They had some blues guy up there, what was his name?
Not Johnny Lee Hooker, but the other guy.
Oh, what's the guy that T-Bone did all the battles with?
No, no, no. You know, the difficult guy that T-bone --
No, it wasn't Wynonie. But this guy, he had bad meter, and then --
Oh, so he was more oldtime, was he, then?
Yes, and a lot of them -- I was just -- the studio would call me, and a lot of people that I don't even remember that I played behind.
Let's see, it was Downbeat label, Marvin -- do you remember Modern Records?
And they had about four or five other labels that came up that you didn't hear anything.
You don't mean PeeWee Craton, do you?
No, no, I remember PeeWee. No, it wasn't PeeWee.

Yeah, I remember, Amos was out there. Yeah, I remember Amos. But I didn't back him up. But it was a lot of people that the names never did do anything, because I was just sort of working with the studio. They'd call me --
Well, what were you doing with the night time? Were you working in clubs?
Well, I was doing pretty good, just recording. So I was just having a ball just recording, and they would pay me double. And they'd pay me double so I didn't do anything but record.
Did they use your name then, every time?
